source.quote: Chord Electronics' own product page for the Qutest, read 2026-11-24, Technical Spec: « USB Type B (White): 44.1kHz to 768kHz - 16bit to 32bit », « 2x BNC Coax (Red): 44.1kHz - 384kHz - 16bit to 32bit », « Optical (Green): 44.1kHz to 96kHz - 16bit to 24bit », « 1x Dual data mode input (using both BNC coax inputs together): 44.1kHz to 768kHz - 16bit to 32bit ». Key Features: « 96kHz Optical Input ». « DSD support: Native playback supported. DSD64 (Single) to DSD512 (Octa-DSD) ». « Chipset: Chord Electronics custom coded Xilinx Artix 7 (XC7A15T) FPGA », « Tap-length: 49,152 », « Pulse array: 10 element pulse array design ».

facts.chip: No commercial converter: « Chord Electronics custom coded Xilinx Artix 7 (XC7A15T) FPGA », with « Tap-length: 49,152 » and a « 10 element pulse array design ». The maker's own design, which is why chord_wta exists as a family - and the case the chip model calls « no commercial chip »: a technology stated, no part number to give.

_dual_data_not_recorded: The page lists « 1x Dual data mode input (using both BNC coax inputs together): 44.1kHz to 768kHz ». That is not a fourth socket but the two BNC inputs used as a pair, and this catalogue has no interface for a mode that consumes two. Recorded here rather than invented as an interface.
